speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome, little one. Since I am your doctor, I must ask you and your parents some questions to help me understand what is wrong. Have you noticed any trouble breathing, a blue tint to your skin, or a very fast heart rate since you were born?

REQUEST TEST: Pulse Oximetry
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no past medical history available. Social history: Mother is a primigravida, no prenatal care received.

speaker: Patient
text: No additional symptoms noted by the mother. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
It seems there may be some confusion, as cellulitis is a bacterial skin infection that is extremely rare and atypical in a newborn without a specific portal of entry like an umbilical stump or skin break. Have you noticed any redness, swelling, or warmth around the umbilical area, or have you observed any pus or discharge?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count
REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive Protein

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Normal newborn health status (Cellulitis ruled out by normal labs and lack of specific skin findings).
